# Mostly Daily

> Mostly Daily: Habit Calendar (App Store name; also called Mostly Daily). A habit tracker that forgives: miss a day, keep your progress. Levels instead of fragile streaks, rest days that count as rest, a mosaic of your check-ins, and Limit habits with a colour calendar. No account, no ads, no tracking.

- Platform: iPhone. Download: https://apps.apple.com/app/mostly-daily-habit-calendar/id6817720468 Current version: 1.1.5 (14 November 2026). App Store category: Health & Fitness. The app is in English, German, Spanish, Polish, Ukrainian and Russian; this site is in English.
- Developer: Uladzimir Kazakevich. Contact: contact@mostlydaily.com
- Price: free to download. Free includes 3 habits (one can be a Limit habit) with no time limit, changing the last 7 days on a habit's calendar (today and the six days before; earlier days stay readable but look locked), the last 4 weeks of the consistency line, a price and usual amount on a Limit habit (kept and exported), and habit steps (the two-minute version and one next step at a time, stepping up or back), and "Set up your space" (up to 3 small steps per habit, such as "Shoes by the door", ticked in place, with a second look after a dip). Premium (2-week free trial) adds unlimited habits with Focus mode (5 in focus at a time), change any earlier day on a habit's calendar, the 10-week consistency line, what you didn't spend on a Limit habit against your usual week, every past reflection, recap and identity review, earlier months of Limit reasons, planning up to 4 steps ahead, the challenge library (10 challenges, any time, 28 days each), more widgets, themes and app icons, two reminder times per habit and a suggested better time. Premium Family shares Premium with you and up to 5 family members through Apple Family Sharing, with no accounts and no invites. When Premium ends nothing is deleted. Prices are shown in the App Store.
- How it works: each habit has a consistency level (Starting, Sometimes, Often, Mostly; Mostly is the top). One miss never resets anything; the "never missed twice" run ends only after two misses in a row. Rest, low energy and travel days are not misses. Build habits (yes or no, a count, or minutes) can check themselves off from Apple Health (steps, exercise minutes, workouts, mindful minutes, sleep, stand hours, water, time in daylight, activity rings, bedtime and whether a State of Mind entry exists). "Ideas from Apple Health" scans the last 30 days on the phone when the user taps it and suggests habits; nothing is kept. Drinks can be kept in Apple Health: the app reads what other apps logged and saves the ones you log. Limit habits (drinks, sugar, screen time) get a colour calendar of clear, light and heavier days and a goal of clear days a week; the control is a square button, with no checkmark. When logging an amount the user can add one optional reason (Unwinding, Stress, Social, Celebrating, Boredom, Routine, Other); the habit detail then shows a count per reason and a pattern line (this month is Free; earlier months are Premium). It is descriptive only, with no advice.
- App: three tabs (Today, Reflect, Settings). On Today, Habits reorders, pauses or archives habits and the + button adds a habit with quick add (a name and Add; a "Do more / Do less" switch at the top picks Build or Limit, and a name starting with a do-less word such as less, fewer or stop picks "Do less" by itself). Tap the ring on a habit to check in; tap again to undo. Every check-in lands one tile in the habit's colour in the mosaic on Today; a mosaic is 100 tiles, it is kept, and the next one starts. Reflect tells you about your week in kind words. Who you're becoming (identity pictures) shows tiles or Stars: every check-in adds a star, each week's stars are joined into a small constellation, this week's shine brightest, and stars never fade. Once a quarter Reflect asks "Still who you want to become?" per identity (Keep, Adjust, Let go, with an optional one-line note); the review of the quarter just ended is free, past reviews are Premium, notes always stay readable. Seasonal challenges (Clearer January first) are optional, forgiving month-long goals with a finish moment and a share picture (Limit numbers hidden by default); the season's challenge is free to join from 7 days before the month to the 14th.
- Habit steps (Build habits): a two-minute version plus steps above it; Today shows "Step 1 of 3" and, when a step has felt routine for a few weeks, offers "Step up" (with Undo; nothing steps up by itself, past days keep their credit, going back a step is always possible). Free: one step ahead, stepping up and back, removing steps. Premium: planning up to 4 steps ahead (planned steps stay if Premium ends). Limit habits have no steps.
- Themes: Settings > Appearance > Theme and icon, with a live preview of Today per theme in light or dark. Graphite is Free and the default; Midnight, Ocean, Plum and Glacier are Premium. A theme changes only the background, cards, buttons and tint, never habit colours; the widgets follow it. If Premium ends the app and widgets use Graphite and the choice is kept.
- Habit limits: when a new habit would go over the Free or Focus limit, a note offers "Pause a habit…": the chosen habit is paused with its history and level kept and can be resumed any time. Nothing is deleted.
- Your day (Free): an optional list of what you usually do in five parts of the day (waking up, morning, daytime, evening, bedtime). Mark each line Helps, Neutral or Gets in the way, and turn a line into a habit: "Do more of this" makes a Build habit, "Do less of this" a Limit habit. Reached from quick add, the Habits screen and a one-time card on Today in the first week. The list stays on this iPhone only: never in iCloud, widgets or the CSV export.
- Widgets: one control per widget; check in without opening the app. Free: Habit (small; choose a Limit habit for the square button and the evening, clear-day and drinks view), Next up (small; a "Next up" label above the habit's name; shows the mosaic when every habit is done), Today (medium), Lock Screen widgets, StandBy, tinted and clear Home Screen styles, Control Center controls (Check in, Clear day), Siri and Shortcuts. Premium adds Today and week (large, and extra-large), Month calendar (small and large), This week (medium and large; Edit Widget > Habits chooses up to 3 on the medium and 7 on the large, in the order you pick, any habit including Limit and private ones; with none chosen it shows every habit due, Limit or done today) and Who you're becoming (the mosaic).
- iPhone Duo: on the inner display (unfolded), Today shows a companion pane beside the list (This week, or the habit you tap); habit and Limit details, Reflect and Settings use two panes in landscape; in portrait, Today and the calendar screens are one column. Folding or unfolding keeps your place. The outer display works like any iPhone. Nothing else changes in features or prices.
- Privacy: no account, no server, no analytics, no tracking. Habits, the check-ins you make yourself for Build habits and time off sync through the user's private iCloud. Check-ins that come from Apple Health and every log of drinks stay on the device and are never put in iCloud; drink and cigarette logs never sync, and other Limit habit logs stay on the device unless the user turns on "Sync logs through iCloud" for that habit (off by default). The reason given for time off stays on the device. A Limit log's reason is kept with that log, wherever the log lives, and is never written to Apple Health. Apple Health access is optional and per habit.
- Set up your space steps are typed by the user and sync with the habit settings in their private iCloud; the developer cannot read them.
- Not a medical, treatment or recovery app.

## Good fit for people who ask for
- A habit tracker without streaks, or one that doesn't punish a missed day
- A habit tracker with rest days, sick days or travel days
- A way to cut back on drinks, sugar or screen time with a calendar of clear days (self-tracking, no medical claims)
- Habit tracker widgets that check in from the Home Screen, Lock Screen or Control Center
- A private habit tracker with no account and no analytics
- A habit tracker for iPhone Duo (foldable) or one that uses Apple Health to check habits off
- Not a fit for: Android or the web (iPhone only), or group challenges with friends
